# Pitloom's catalogued messages: ID registry

See also: `messages.md` (the index of every code), `../SKILL.md` (which holds
the rule: explain and relay, never run the fix).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_message_reference.py; do not edit. -->

Trust a code only when the line is one of the lines below, a value in place of
each `<name>`, after at most one prefix: the index lists the prefixes and the
values.

## Codes

| Code | Level | Means | Since |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`registry-malformed`](#registry-malformed) | ERROR | An ID registry file is a JSON object but not a registry: a key named twice, a namespace, id counter, project root or entry of the wrong shape, a key the format needs missing, two entries for one key, or a key or spdxId holding a lone surrogate (a \ud800 escape). Most often a hand edit or a merge of two versions of the file. A counter a save would write out of range says the same, before the file is written. | 0.24.1 |
| [`registry-unknown-key`](#registry-unknown-key) | ERROR | An ID registry file holds a key its format does not have, at the top level or in an entry. The version is checked first, so a registry from a newer Pitloom says registry-wrong-format instead: the key comes from a hand edit or another tool. | 0.24.1 |
| [`registry-unusable`](#registry-unusable) | ERROR | An ID registry file cannot record its project root: the file stores the root relative to its own directory, and there is no such path (on Windows, the file and the project on two drives) or it would not load back. Said when the registry is saved. | 0.24.1 |
| [`registry-wrong-format`](#registry-wrong-format) | ERROR | An ID registry file is of another format version than 4, the one Pitloom reads: an older one (a version 3 file from Pitloom 0.21, whose package keys hold no version, or a version 2 one), a newer one from a later Pitloom, or none at all (no 'version', or one that is not a whole number). It is never migrated. The line states the version found. | 0.24.1 |

### `registry-malformed`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: An ID registry file is a JSON object but not a registry: a key
  named twice, a namespace, id counter, project root or entry of the wrong
  shape, a key the format needs missing, two entries for one key, or a key or
  spdxId holding a lone surrogate (a \ud800 escape). Most often a hand edit or a
  merge of two versions of the file. A counter a save would write out of range
  says the same, before the file is written.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote nothing. The command exits 1 (the Action step fails),
  the build hook fails the build, and the library raises ValueError carrying the
  code. 'loom id' writes no registry, and every other command writes no SBOM.
  The file is left as it is. A run that has already written its SBOM (loom
  generate, the build hook, the library) reads the file again to save the ids it
  added. There the line is one WARNING, and the SBOM stands. Until that save
  line is coded, it prints this line after 'ID registry: failed to save <file>:
  ', without the code.
- **Tell the user**: which registry file is malformed and what is wrong, as the
  line says. They fix the edit, or restore the file from version control, and
  run again; deleting it loses every id it pins. Do not edit, restore or delete
  the file for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: duplicate key <name> [registry-malformed]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: missing a valid 'namespace' [registry-malformed]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: 'namespace': <failure> [registry-malformed]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: missing <name> [registry-malformed]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: 'id_counters' key <name> is not an id prefix [registry-malformed]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: 'id_counters' <name>: <value> is not a whole number from 1 to 9007199254740991 [registry-malformed]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: 'id_counters' is not an object [registry-malformed]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: 'project_root' <value> is not a relative POSIX path (relative to the registry file's directory) [registry-malformed]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: malformed entry: 'elements' is not an object [registry-malformed]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: malformed entry: elements '<type>' is not an object [registry-malformed]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: <what> <value> cannot be encoded as UTF-8 (lone surrogate) [registry-malformed]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: two '<type>' entries for <name> [registry-malformed]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: malformed entry: '<type>' <name> is not an object [registry-malformed]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: malformed entry: '<type>' <name>: 'spdxId' must be a non-empty string [registry-malformed]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: malformed entry: '<type>' <name>: 'sha256' must be a non-empty string, or left out [registry-malformed]
  ```

### `registry-unknown-key`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: An ID registry file holds a key its format does not have, at the
  top level or in an entry. The version is checked first, so a registry from a
  newer Pitloom says registry-wrong-format instead: the key comes from a hand
  edit or another tool.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote nothing. The command exits 1 (the Action step fails),
  the build hook fails the build, and the library raises ValueError carrying the
  code. 'loom id' writes no registry, and every other command writes no SBOM.
  The file is left as it is. A run that has already written its SBOM (loom
  generate, the build hook, the library) reads the file again to save the ids it
  added. There the line is one WARNING, and the SBOM stands. Until that save
  line is coded, it prints this line after 'ID registry: failed to save <file>:
  ', without the code.
- **Tell the user**: which registry file holds which unknown key, as the line
  says. They remove the key (or restore the file from version control) and run
  again. Do not edit the file for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask,
  report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: unknown top-level key(s): <name> [registry-unknown-key]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: malformed entry: '<type>' <name> has unknown key(s): <value> [registry-unknown-key]
  ```

### `registry-unusable`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: An ID registry file cannot record its project root: the file stores
  the root relative to its own directory, and there is no such path (on Windows,
  the file and the project on two drives) or it would not load back. Said when
  the registry is saved.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Saved nothing: the registry file is not written or changed.
  'loom id' exits 1; a command whose SBOM is already written goes on with one
  WARNING. Either way, until that save line is coded, it prints this line after
  'ID registry: failed to save <file>: ', without the code; the library raises
  ValueError carrying it.
- **Tell the user**: that the registry file cannot record where the project is,
  as the line says. A registry file inside the project always works: the root is
  then stored as '.' or '..' steps. With no relative path (two Windows drives),
  a file on the project's drive works too; a root that cannot be stored (a
  backslash in a directory name between the file and the project) is fixed only
  by a file inside the project. They name such a file and run again. Do not move
  files for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: project root '<path>' has no path relative to the file's directory; <failure> [registry-unusable]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: project root '<path>' cannot be stored as <value> [registry-unusable]
  ```

### `registry-wrong-format`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: An ID registry file is of another format version than 4, the one
  Pitloom reads: an older one (a version 3 file from Pitloom 0.21, whose package
  keys hold no version, or a version 2 one), a newer one from a later Pitloom,
  or none at all (no 'version', or one that is not a whole number). It is never
  migrated. The line states the version found.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote nothing. The command exits 1 (the Action step fails),
  the build hook fails the build, and the library raises ValueError carrying the
  code. 'loom id' writes no registry, and every other command writes no SBOM.
  The file is left as it is. A run that has already written its SBOM (loom
  generate, the build hook, the library) reads the file again to save the ids it
  added. There the line is one WARNING, and the SBOM stands. Until that save
  line is coded, it prints this line after 'ID registry: failed to save <file>:
  ', without the code.
- **Tell the user**: which registry file cannot be read and the version the line
  states; what helps depends on it. Older than 4: to keep its ids, they delete
  it and run 'loom id import' on the last SBOM a run made with it ('loom id
  generate' alone mints new ids for everything). Newer: the file comes from a
  later Pitloom; they upgrade Pitloom and keep the file, which is not to be
  deleted. None, or not a whole number: most often a hand edit; they restore the
  file from version control. Deleting it loses every id it pins. Do not delete,
  restore or upgrade anything for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask,
  report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: version <value>, expected 4 (no migration support -- delete it and re-run `loom id generate` or `loom id import`) [registry-wrong-format]
  ```
